summary.headline: KPIT Q1 FY27: constant-currency revenue grew only 0.1% YoY and fell 3.6% QoQ, with EBITDA margin at 17.2% and PAT at INR 1.17 billion.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was roughly flat YoY in constant currency (+0.1%) and down 0.6% YoY in USD, with QoQ constant-currency revenue down 3.6%, against management's earlier guide of about 1% YoY degrowth and about 5% QoQ decline. Profitability fell more than proportionally: EBITDA margin was 17.2%, EBIT margin 12.3%, and PAT INR 1.17 billion, hit by forex losses and a share of losses from Qorix tied to postponed European revenues. Deal wins were USD 257 million, led by connected cars, aftersales transformation and autonomous. Management guided H2 better than H1, with a return to growth by Q4, and said margin recovery will largely follow revenue recovery.

financial_highlights.change: QoQ decline of about 4.5% in USD terms (per analyst question, not disputed by management)
Hit by forex loss and share of loss from Qorix
Led by connected cars, aftersales transformation and autonomous

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue impact about 4% for the quarter from postponed revenues; more than 50% of KPIT revenue comes from Europe. Management expects the impact to show up in Q2 at a regional level.

segments.name: Americas (US)
segments.commentary: Growth described as fairly well balanced across the portfolio, with good CV growth and long-standing passenger car relationships; management expects growth to continue.

segments.name: SIMA (Southeast Asia, India, Middle East, Africa)
segments.commentary: Management said SIMA showed a sharp drop this quarter off a small base, but described significant growth there.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Revenue fell more than other segments because of a one-time large license deal in the prior quarter that did not recur; management expects CV growth in Q2 and Q3.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: Revenue declined about 3.5 million in the quarter; management said PV growth expected but did not materialise, and two accounts (one Japan SDV program cancelled, one Europe SDV program ending) are stabilising by Q3.

guidance_outlook: H2 expected to be better than H1; return to growth by Q4 led by Q4 performance.
Q2 revenue expected to be flattish QoQ, per management's June update as reconfirmed on the call; Europe impact to be visible in Q2.
Margins to improve incrementally, not significantly, until revenue returns to growth; Qorix losses expected to continue for at least one or two more quarters.

Management did not commit to a specific Q4 margin level; asked whether a return to 20%+ EBITDA by Q4 is the working assumption, the CEO said it depends on growth and European cost take-out takes longer.
Medium-term margin aspiration of 22% to 24% by FY29 (from Analyst Day) reiterated as achievable, driven by products and solutions growth and outcome-based models.
Q4 growth comparison basis was not firmly defined: management said Q-on-Q for growth turnaround, with Q4 margin level 'flattish' per the CEO.
risks_watch: Timing of European pipeline conversion into revenue; management said wins are not in question but start dates are uncertain.
Europe cost take-out is slower than other regions, delaying margin recovery.
Continued Qorix share of losses for at least one or two quarters.
Q2 revenue flattish and Europe impact visible in Q2; Q3 stabilisation of the SDV-linked accounts depends on delivery.
Wage increases deferred this year; management said increments will be given in stages, starting with younger grades.
summary.management_tone: Candid but cautious: management acknowledged a weak quarter and that European and Japanese OEM disruption created uncertainty, repeating the H2-over-H1 and Q4 growth timeline. Answers on margin timing and Q4 growth basis were less specific, and management pointed to pipeline and wins rather than firm numbers.
key_quotes: What we are not sure in the case of the current part is when these deals will realize.
So revenue will be the major driver.
I think the learning from the recent challenges with Japan and Germany is, I think we just need to have a lot more intensity and we have to run faster.

qa_highlights.question: When will commercial vehicles return to growth, and is the Europe weakness temporary given strong Europe deal wins and OEM model launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor Patil said the weakness is not permanent; CV was hit by a one-time large license deal in the prior quarter and growth is expected next quarter. He said the uncertainty is about when deals will realise, not whether KPIT gets its share.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 22% to 24% margin aspiration for FY29 from the Analyst Day still hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor Patil said the medium-term outlook remains good, with product and solutions revenue expected to grow and be margin accretive, and some solutions ready to deploy in the next quarter or two; outcome-based models are also part of the plan.

qa_highlights.question: Can you unpack US growth between OEMs and off-highway, and is the momentum sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Chinmay Pandit said US growth is fairly balanced across the portfolio, with good CV growth and long-standing passenger car relationships, and visibility for the coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Europe impact show up in Q2, and what is the Europe revenue quantum?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor Patil said Europe impact was about 4% of quarterly revenue, will show up in Q2 at a regional level, and will be offset by US and SIMA growth at company level. He said SIMA dropped sharply this quarter off a small base.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise sharply this quarter, and what is the margin trajectory for the next three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyamvada Hardikar said the increase reflects forex impact on consolidated accounts, provisions linked to acquisitions, and subcontracting costs in the European region, all operational. Kishor Patil said margins will improve incrementally, not significantly, until revenue returns to growth, and Qorix losses will continue for at least one or two more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q2 flattish, Q3 growing and Q4 significant growth still the assumption, and is 20%+ EBITDA by Q4 the working assumption?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor Patil said the large part depends on growth. European cost take-out will take much longer than other regions, so margins return once revenue grows. He said Q4 growth would be measured Q-on-Q and Q4 level would be flattish.

capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were given on the call; the only investment reference was to batteries, where management said a sodium-ion pilot plant needs more than USD 100 million of investment and about two to three years before production, with royalties only after production milestones.
Management said wage increments are being deferred this year and will be given in stages, starting with younger grades, with senior staff to follow over time.
Management said the Caresoft acquisition is being used for cost-reduction programmes for existing OEMs, and provisions relating to acquisitions were cited as a driver of higher other expenses in Q1.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 constant-currency revenue grew 0.1% YoY and fell 3.6% QoQ; USD revenue fell 0.6% YoY. Management had earlier guided about 1% YoY degrowth and about 5% QoQ decline.

Deal wins were USD 257 million in the quarter, led by connected cars, aftersales transformation and autonomous. Management said wins are not in question and the issue is the timing of revenue start dates, especially in Europe.

Europe impact was about 4% of quarterly revenue from postponed revenues; management said the impact will show at a regional level in Q2, offset by growth in the US and SIMA. More than 50% of revenue comes from Europe.

Commercial vehicles fell more than other segments because of a one-time large license deal in the prior quarter that did not recur; management expects CV growth in Q2 and Q3. Passenger vehicle revenue fell about 3.5 million, with one Japan SDV program cancelled and one Europe SDV program ending, both expected to stabilise in Q3.

Management said the Europe OEM conversation has shifted to helping clients cut product cost by 30% to 40% and production cost, with revenue from these initiatives expected after the next couple of quarters. Pipeline growth areas cited were off-highway (seven new OEMs), trucks and bus (four OEMs), and new passenger car OEMs in Korea, Europe, US and Japan.
Strategic clients were about 87% of Q1 revenue and the management clarified the 84% figure is the share of the prior quarter's revenue, with QoQ strategic-client decline of 1.3%.

growth.why: Q1 FY27 cc revenue grew only 0.1% YoY and fell 3.6% QoQ; management guides H2 above H1 with a return to growth by Q4 and Q2 flattish QoQ, but no revenue growth % is given, no capacity or capex was announced (sodium-ion pilot is only a discussed >USD 100m option), and margins will improve only incrementally.
